items.text: Go to Accessibility tool – run scan
Notice that manually created form fields will not be tagged and will have errors in Tagged Annotations and Forms

content.description: Screenshot of the NVDA context menu. The main menu items are Preferences, Tools, Help, Configuration profiles, Revert to saved configuration, Reset configuration to factory defaults, Save configuration, Donate, and Exit. The 'Preferences' menu is expanded to show a submenu containing 'Settings...', 'Speech dictionaries', 'Punctuation/symbol pronunciation...', and 'Input gestures...'.

Screenshot of the 'NVDA Settings: Speech (normal configuration)' dialog box. The left pane lists Categories, with 'Speech' selected. The right pane shows the Synthesizer set to 'Windows OneCore voices'. Below this, an orange rectangle highlights the Voice settings: a 'Voice' dropdown set to 'Microsoft Zira', sliders for 'Rate', 'Pitch', and 'Volume', and a 'Punctuation/symbol level' dropdown set to 'none'. Checked options include 'Automatic language switching', 'Trust voice's language when processing characters and symbols', 'Include Unicode Consortium data', and 'Use spelling functionality if supported'. Unchecked options include 'Rate boost', 'Automatic dialect switching', 'Delayed descriptions for characters on cursor movement', 'Say cap before capitals', and 'Beep for capitals'. A 'Capital pitch change percentage' is set to 30. Buttons for OK, Cancel, and Apply are at the bottom.
Screenshot of the NVDA software menu showing 'Preferences' selected, which expands a submenu where 'Settings...' is highlighted.
Screenshot of the NVDA Settings dialog box open to the 'Mouse' category. A red outline highlights the 'Enable mouse tracking' checkbox to emphasize it.
Screenshot of the NVDA screen reader context menu. The 'Tools' option is selected, which opens a secondary submenu where the 'Speech viewer' option is highlighted.

Screenshot of the NVDA Speech Viewer dialog window. The text inside the viewer reads 'How to Test with NVDA in Windows.pptx - PowerPoint Slide 4 (Enable Speech Viewer) - Slide view'. At the bottom of the window is an unchecked box labeled 'Show Speech Viewer on Startup'.
